findings.detail: If git emits the main worktree record and then exits nonzero before listing another live worktree, live_worktrees_json returns success with the truncated inventory. decorate_claims consequently marks the omitted worktree's claim stale; check reports its resource free, claim can replace it without approval, and prune can delete it. This predates the change and is explicitly deferred in the audit ledger, but the new exception leaves the consequential failure in place.
findings.evidence: The process substitution at line 230 exposes no producer status. Any emitted field sets saw_any=1, and the final jq returns success. Lines 507-524 then set live_known=yes and mark absent holders stale. cmd_claim permits replacing stale claims at lines 826-851; cmd_prune removes them at lines 954-963. main_worktree_path at line 126 has the same unchecked producer, whereas launch-workmux:129 checks the captured command's status.
findings.title: Absent or partial data: failed worktree inventory can release live resource claims

findings.detail: The validator accepts multiple concatenated issue objects instead of requiring one object. For example, stdin containing {"number":1,"title":"One","state":"OPEN"} followed by {"number":2,"title":"Two","state":"OPEN"} passes validation and exits successfully with numbers and titles concatenated into a malformed single-issue prompt. This predates the change.
findings.evidence: jq empty accepts a JSON stream, and jq -e 'type == "object"' succeeds for the two objects. jq_value processes both documents, so number becomes "1\n2" and title becomes "One\nTwo" before the single printf in main. The sibling read_claims implementation explicitly counts documents with jq -s 'length' at lines 292-299 and rejects more than one.
findings.title: Validator gaps: concatenated issue objects pass the single-object validation

findings.detail: The new exception reasons claim that suppressed errors receive replacement diagnostics, but those diagnostics do not exist. remove_file_if_present only returns failure after an unsuccessful rm; its callers emit no cleanup-specific diagnostic. Similarly, the new comment at line 233 promises a contextual diagnostic when resolving a worktree directory fails, but that branch silently returns success and skips prompt delivery. The comments should describe the actual handling.
findings.evidence: Lines 69-73 discard rm stderr and return a filesystem predicate. All remove_file_if_present call sites lack a cleanup diagnostic; run_workmux_and_cleanup_prompt returns the saved workmux status after cleanup. Lines 233-234 return 0 on failed cd, and send_prompt_to_codex_pane treats the resulting empty pane ID as a silent no-op at lines 268-270.
findings.title: Docs drift: exception reasons promise diagnostics that are never emitted
